records.text: The user loves the idea of decorating their house with lights and ornaments for Diwali.

Traditional Diwali decorations include diyas and candles; rangoli made with colored rice, sand, or powder; flowers such as marigolds, roses, and lotuses; torans made from mango leaves, marigolds, or other materials; multicolored fairy lights; wall hangings featuring deities or traditional symbols and patterns; and paper or metal lanterns.

Diwali attire varies by region and culture: in northern India, women commonly wear colorful sarees or salwar-kameez and men kurta pyjamas or sherwanis; in southern India, women wear silk sarees and men dhotis with silk or cotton shirts. Traditional jewelry such as bangles and earrings may also be worn. Western clothing is generally acceptable, though attendees should follow any dress code set by a Diwali event.

Diwali traditions may include lighting diyas and candles, making rangoli, cleaning and decorating homes, exchanging sweets, snacks, and gifts, performing puja to Lakshmi and Ganesha, fireworks, and sharing elaborate meals. Lighting is described as symbolizing the victory of good over evil; puja seeks blessings for wealth, prosperity, happiness, and good fortune.
